title: Native class-group platform product
objective: Package the production resident class-group executable lazily in supported native platform packages, authenticate and supervise it from a coarse JavaScript client, and prove relocation, corruption, crash, and fallback behavior

oracles: Production service protocol tests and native-versus-Wasm receipt parity

handoff.summary: Packages an optional authenticated class-group-service and its lazy CommonJS client in supported native platform archives. The client verifies the closed manifest and exact executable hash before spawn, performs the ABI-1 capability handshake before exposing backend.call, serializes resident requests, retires crashed processes without replay, and rejects stale sessions. Focused tests cover relocation, absent and corrupt artifacts, process restart, close semantics, the legacy two-executable packager call, optional archive contents, and the explicit Windows fallback.
risks: The real Rust service is supplied by the dependent class-group-product-service lane; this lane currently qualifies transport and lifecycle against a deterministic protocol fixture.

The integration branch portable suite passes this lane but currently fails a pre-existing modular q-expansion source-freeze comparison; the full build also stops on an unrelated numerical production-manifest toolchain identity mismatch.
Native release artifacts still require qualification on Linux arm64 and macOS arm64; Windows intentionally uses the non-native fallback.
next_steps: Merge class-group-product-service, build target/release/class-group-service, and pass that path as the optional fourth argument to scripts/build-npm-platform-package.cjs on qualified Linux and macOS release hosts.
Have the runtime host load the platform package's ./class-groups export and consume createNativeClassGroupBackend; fall back when it returns undefined.
Run real-service protocol parity and relocation tests, then add the optional service argument to release staging for Linux and macOS only.
